The document "Perspectives on the relationship between materials chemistry and roll-to-roll electrode manufacturing for high-energy lithium-ion batteries" (ensm-2020) does not provide a specific cost per kWh for the NFA 811 pouch cell. However, it mentions that the NFA cathode material was initially synthesized as hydroxide precursors using the co-precipitation process in a continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR) followed by calcination in oxygen-rich atmospheres to obtain the final cathode material. The obtained material was coated onto aluminum current collectors using the slot-die coating process. Full pouch cells were assembled using conventional graphite anodes and Argonne National Laboratory "Gen 2" electrolyte.

The paper does provide a comparison of the cost of cobalt in the cathodes for different battery technologies. For the same pack energies, the amount of cobalt required for each of these cathode classes estimated using the BatPaC program is shown in Figure 1B.
